market_brief: Asia finished the Nvidia-led squeeze with big gains in data/latest.json (Taiwan +9.0%, Kospi +6.3% above 5,000, Nikkei +3.9%) while Hong Kong fell 0.7%, but Europe stalled (STOXX 600 flat, DAX -0.3%) and US futures are giving some back, with Nasdaq futures about 1% lower and Nvidia down nearly 5% premarket. Sanofi's $41bn Insmed deal is the day's big M&A story; hawkish central-bank talk continues (ECB's Simkus joins Williams and Pill), and prediction markets put a December Fed hike near 94% with the 10-year at 4.92% and DXY at 104.2. Commodities are mixed: Brent sits near $86.6 and copper (-1.7%), silver (-3.2%) and gold (-0.9% to ~$3,618) are softer, while US natural gas jumped 13.6% on a cold snap; bitcoin is back under $60k (-2.2%). Consumer confidence, a 5-year auction and Dell/HP/Workday/Autodesk earnings come today, ahead of Wednesday's PCE and GDP and India's reopening after Monday's 1.75% Nifty drop.
ai_brief: Zhipu's GLM-5.4 adds a looped-layer design and million-token context, and AWS rolled out trusted-access tooling with Anthropic's enterprise safeguards plus open Gemma-based decision models. A reported Claude-generated complexity-theory proof awaits human review, while Meta's TLX kernels and an agent-designed CPU show AI pushing further into the hardware stack.

items.headline: US futures give back part of Monday's surge; Nvidia down nearly 5% premarket
items.summary: Nasdaq futures were about 1% lower and S&P futures 0.4% lower before the open, with Nvidia off about 4.8% after Monday's 31% jump. Tech (XLK) was down about 2% premarket while defensives such as healthcare and staples gained.

items.headline: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed for $175 a share, about $41bn in cash
items.summary: Sanofi will fund the deal with debt and cash, expects it to be EPS-accretive by end-2028 and sees closing in H1 2027; Insmed's Brinsupri has booked $1.09bn in 2026 sales so far. Sanofi shares rose about 5.6% in Paris, per Reuters.

items.headline: European stocks pause after their best day since May; miners and chip names slip
items.summary: The STOXX 600 was roughly flat to slightly lower as Monday's tech rally faded, with miners down about 3% (Anglo American and Antofagasta over 5%) as copper and gold eased. Compass rose 3.7% on organic growth and Kingfisher fell 4% on weak France and Poland trading.

items.headline: UBS cuts Aixtron to Sell; shares fall almost 9%
items.summary: Aixtron dropped about 8.8% after UBS downgraded the chip-equipment maker to Sell, dragging Infineon and ASM International down over 2%.

items.headline: German Ifo edges up to 90.6, slightly above forecasts
items.summary: November business climate rose to 90.6 (consensus 90.5) and current conditions to 89.4, while expectations held at 91.6, just below the 92.0 forecast.

items.headline: ECB's Simkus says more tightening may be needed in 2027
items.summary: Governing Council member Simkus said further hikes could be required next year if inflation persists, adding to a hawkish week that included Williams at the Fed and Pill at the BoE.

items.headline: Prediction markets price about 94% odds of a 25bp Fed hike on Dec 9
items.summary: Kalshi and Polymarket's international book both showed roughly 93.5% for a quarter-point hike at Monday's close, with CME futures implying about 96%; a 50bp move gets about 5%, per a third-party tracker.

items.headline: China extends pause on some critical-mineral export curbs to the US until Jan 27
items.summary: Beijing kept its ban on US-bound gallium, germanium and antimony on hold rather than letting the pause lapse on Friday. Separately, the EU imposed provisional import quotas on hybrid vehicles.

items.headline: Update: HPE falls about 12% premarket despite raised guidance; Semtech also drops
items.summary: What changed: HPE's after-hours slip deepened to about 12.5% premarket after a 17% Monday gain, despite its FY27 guide and $5bn buyback addition. Semtech fell about 12.6% after a Q3 beat.

items.headline: Analog Devices reports record fiscal Q4, beating estimates
items.summary: Analog Devices reported record fourth-quarter results before the open, with revenue up about 42% year on year, per AlphaStreet. Shares reaction was not yet clear at the time of writing.

items.headline: Jacobs guides FY27 EPS to $8.05-8.45; Dollar Tree and Burlington rise premarket
items.summary: Jacobs' fiscal Q4 adjusted EPS rose about 26% to $2.20 with backlog up 24% to $28.7bn. Dollar Tree gained about 8% and Burlington about 6% premarket after results, while Agilent held a near-7% gain.

items.headline: Copper slides below $12,200 while gas jumps on a northern European cold snap
items.summary: LME copper fell about 3.6% and gold eased toward $3,610, while Dutch TTF firmed to EUR 88-92/MWh on forecasts of prolonged cold and below-average storage; US natural gas futures rose about 13%.

items.headline: Update: Iran's army chief reportedly orders Hormuz kept closed until seven conditions are met
items.summary: What changed: Iran's army chief Hatami reportedly ordered the strait to stay shut pending Tehran's conditions, even as Qatar's PM met Vance and Rubio to revive talks. Brent held near a three-month low around $89 as Libyan and Gulf supply returns.

items.headline: Japan's services PMI slows to 50.5; government downgrades consumer-spending view
items.summary: Japan's flash manufacturing PMI rose to 53.7 but services slipped to 50.5 from 51.7; Kyodo reports Tokyo may ease FX special-account rules to fund tax cuts. USD/JPY traded near 159.5.

items.headline: Options: Monday's rally used 120% of the S&P's priced weekly range; Nvidia saw 11m+ contracts
items.summary: Saxo notes the VIX fell about 26% to 26.6 and one-day implied vol nearly halved, yet the S&P is still about 5% below its 50-day average. More than 11 million Nvidia options traded Monday, about 6.7 million of them calls, per Current Logic.

items.headline: French bonds outperform and dollar holds a 19-month high vs the euro
items.summary: CaixaBank notes French spreads narrowed about 6bp after Macron's budget-rule proposal, while US front-end yields edged up and the 10-year held near 4.9%.

items.headline: Week ahead: consumer confidence and 5-year auction today; PCE and GDP Wednesday; US shut Thursday
items.summary: Dell, HP, Workday and Autodesk report after Tuesday's close. Wednesday brings October PCE (core seen 3.2% y/y) and Q3 GDP (seen 3.4%) plus India's reopening after the Guru Nanak Jayanti holiday; US markets close Thursday and shorten Friday, and the Fed meets Dec 8-9.

items.headline: Zhipu releases GLM-5.4 with a looped-transformer design and 1M-token context
items.summary: Z.ai says GLM-5.4 repeats selected layers to improve reasoning, adds image input and a million-token window, and expands Coding Plan allowances.

items.headline: AWS launches a Trusted Access API on Bedrock with Anthropic's Enterprise Frontier Safeguards in preview
items.summary: The API lets enterprises enrol in trusted-access programmes via IAM; Anthropic's safeguards flag coordinated misuse across requests and produce Safety Case reports without retaining customer data.

items.headline: AWS open-sources Strands Decider v2 decision models built on Gemma 4
items.summary: Five Apache-2.0 models from 2B to 31B parameters target agent routing decisions; AWS reports large labelling-cost and latency savings in internal ticketing and also released a sandbox CLI for coding agents.

items.headline: Anthropic reportedly claims a Claude-generated proof that VP differs from VNP
items.summary: A 70-page paper with a Lean 4 formalisation claims superpolynomial lower bounds for circuits computing the permanent; it has not yet been reviewed by human mathematicians and does not address P vs NP, per RIO Rundown.

items.headline: Meta releases TLX, low-level Triton extensions for Hopper, Blackwell and MI300
items.summary: TLX gives Python kernels warp-group control; Meta self-reports matmul performance within a few percent of cuBLAS on H100.

items.headline: Architect Labs unveils Frostbite, an agent-designed CPU core
items.summary: The startup claims 4.6x performance per watt versus a modern in-order core in pre-silicon tests, with agents verifying the design; results are not yet on silicon.

items.headline: GlobalFoundries expands Spot rollout and becomes an early Atlas test customer
items.summary: Spot robots will spread to GlobalFoundries fabs in the US, Germany and Singapore after 90,000+ inspections; Atlas testing is slated from early 2027, per RIO Rundown.

items.headline: AMD-powered Lux supercomputer at Oak Ridge debuts at No. 14 on the TOP500
items.summary: Built with HPE on EPYC CPUs and MI355X GPUs, Lux targets fusion and materials research under the DOE's Genesis Mission.

items.headline: Supreme Court Justice Bagchi floats AI-assisted courts for routine divorce applications
items.summary: Speaking at a DNLU conclave, he suggested 24/7 AI handling of routine filings to ease a backlog of over five crore cases; it is a proposal, not policy.

items.headline: Nvidia and Paradromics show brain-implant speech AI in a clinical trial
items.summary: A trial participant used a brain implant and AI decoding to talk with her grandchildren; the firms aim to make conversations faster and more natural.

items.headline: What AI newsletters are focused on: Huang's return, PR-review agents and Grok lawsuits
items.summary: Tuesday's digests lead with Nvidia reinstating Huang, Anthropic's Claude Ship code-review agents and the Oregon/Virginia suits over Grok images, alongside GLM-5.4 and AWS's safety tooling.
